### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/getting-started/examples.mdx`  _(via artifactFlows (symbol, a field of interface DefineStackOptions))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via validateWidgetBindings (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via validateWidgetBindings (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `defineStack (literal, 74 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 10b8250ad5af331beed721694dca6e43df6d16b8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `56d41b252e302762e1cb39ec610fd5e779e8036f` — the merge of head `45b786764e97c05431a870693d2345b247833163` into base `10b8250ad5af331beed721694dca6e43df6d16b8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 56d41b252e302762e1cb39ec610fd5e779e8036f && git checkout 56d41b252e302762e1cb39ec610fd5e779e8036f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 10b8250ad5af331beed721694dca6e43df6d16b8 45b786764e97c05431a870693d2345b247833163 && git checkout -B drift-repro 10b8250ad5af331beed721694dca6e43df6d16b8 && git merge --no-ff 45b786764e97c05431a870693d2345b247833163

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 10b8250ad5af331beed721694dca6e43df6d16b8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 10b8250ad5af331beed721694dca6e43df6d16b8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · #25514 · `domain:spec` seat 2 (seat post #18549) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_01PC4NPXPgPmpDRG9DdDnyXT` · 2026-10-24T09:58Z · head `45b786764e` · report `6382768493` · seat review at `TIER_DEFAULT`. The clause-② enqueue gate hits on both limbs (path: `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`; declaration: `Clause-②: yes`), so a same-shape `## Contract review` PASS at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the landing head is still owed. `needs:contract-review` is added in this stroke.

1. **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #25514`, no other closing keyword. `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added` and `Ruling-ref: 6377677280` are line-initial in the body. The changeset carries both declarations, with `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/lint` at `minor`. Six files, +523/−16 (`get_files`): `stack.zod.ts`, `validate-widget-bindings.ts`, two new test files, the changeset, and `content/docs/getting-started/examples.mdx`. No governed path, no `content/docs/releases/`. The PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (the relay).
2. **Ruling, measured on the diff.** Ruling A asks that a reference resolve against the artifact, and that a name no package defines stay refused. Defect 1: one `checkFlowTarget` now serves the three positions (top-level, object-bound, inline page). A target in `artifactFlows` passes only where it used to be refused (own `flows` non-empty), and is recorded as a claim. `composeStacks` refuses a claim that no input defines (`collectArtifactFlowClaimErrors`, reading each input's `flows` and its `packages[]` bodies), with the same per-finding message. A target in neither scope is refused as before. Defect 2: `widget-dataset-unknown` adds the `packages[]` bodies' datasets to the resolution map only; dataset-level checks still walk `stack.datasets`; the stack's own name wins. Ruling note (2), the booted measurement, is in the PR body: the sibling flow started from the action (HTTP 200, one row written), and the sibling dataset returned 2 rows to the widget query.
3. **Gates.** Check-runs on `45b786764e` at this record: 25 success, 6 skipped, 9 in progress, 0 failed. Local, per the report: `--ran` 113/113 with no NOT MEASURED; spec 715 files and lint 159 files green; cli unit 327/327; metadata-protocol's three publish-gate files 24/24. Ablations: spec claim branch 5/9 red, compose pass 1/9 red, lint loop 3/6 red plus `objectstack validate` exiting 1 at the door. Landing waits for every check green and the contract-review PASS.
4. **Deviations accepted.** (a) `content/docs/getting-started/examples.mdx` (+9) is outside the claim's declared surface. It is disclosed in the PR's Acceptance notes but not as a report deviation. It is accepted as the page that restates the multi-package split rules. I checked its two sentences against the diff: "in a composition of two or more packages, `composeStacks` refuses a claimed flow that no package defines" matches `collectArtifactFlowClaimErrors` and the option's own boundary; "`os build`, `os validate` and `os lint` resolve it against every package of the artifact, and still refuse a dataset that no package declares" matches the lint hunk on the per-package pass, which carries `packages[]`. (b) The verification shape is a recorded claim, not the `artifactObjects`-style re-run (the report's `open_questions` item). Accepted: a re-run would newly refuse a `strict: false` input, an undeclared narrowing. The contract review answers it as a boundary flag. (c) One `origin/main` merge (`e649c2d91e`), re-tested. `mcp_calls` 0; relay writes 2.
5. **Out-of-scope outcomes.**
   - `indexObjectGraph` reads `stack.objects` only, so on the per-package pass a widget filter over a sibling-owned dataset's object is skipped as unknowable (not refused); the union run still judges it: Acceptance notes (a read-only observation with no wrong answer measured at a door).
   - HotCRM must add `artifactFlows` to its app package's `defineStack`; its unblock is a release carrying this: carried by objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2270 (the seat posts the pointer there at merge).
6. **Landing.** Not governed, 539 changed lines. Once the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS is on record and every check on the then-current head is green, the seat sends `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `45b786764e97c05431a870693d2345b247833163`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/stack-provenance.ts, packages/spec/src/stack-artifact-flow-crossref.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-widget-bindings.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-widget-bindings.artifact-datasets.test.ts, packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts (`packagesOf`, `recordsOf`; not in the diff), packages/cli/src/utils/artifact-packages.ts (`packageBodyAsStack`; not in the diff), packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-gate.ts and runtime-authoring-gate.ts (not in the diff), .changeset/25514-artifact-flow-dataset-refs.md, content/docs/getting-started/examples.mdx. The remainder of the diff outside the schema face is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT` (card comment 6382832757).

Inputs, and nothing else: card #25514 (body and every comment; ruling of record 6377677280; dev report 6382768493), PR #25617 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at merge-base `e649c2d91e`), and the check-runs on the head. Read-only: nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong:

1. **`defineStack` accept set — widened, opt-in, byte-identical without the option. RIGHT.** `validateCrossReferences` takes `artifactFlows` and `flowClaims`; one `checkFlowTarget` closure serves the three positions (`actions[]`, `objects[].actions[]`, inline page actions). Its guard — no target, own `flows` empty, or target in own `flows` ⇒ return — is the former inline condition inverted, so the plugin leniency and every refusal that exists today are unchanged; a target in `artifactFlows` is accepted and recorded where it was refused. `flowNames` has no other consumer at the head (lines 4267 to 4280 only), so no flow-reference site is left on the old scope.
2. **Refusal text — byte-identical. RIGHT.** `flowTargetMessage(subject, target)` reproduces the three former literals exactly (`Action 'x'`, `Action 'x' on object 'o'`, the inline `where`), and the new test pins all three strings. No runtime string carries a tracker number.
3. **Public surface — one additive member. RIGHT.** `DefineStackOptions.artifactFlows?: readonly string[]`, optional, on an exported interface. `DefineStackOptions` has no Zod mirror (the only options schema is `ComposeStacksOptionsSchema`) and `defineStack` hands `options` straight to `buildDefinedStack`, so the key is neither stripped nor refused. No `api-surface/` shard moves: the snapshot records that an export exists, not its members, and `TypeScript Type Check` — the job hosting every spec generated-artifact gate — is green on the head.
4. **The claim record — not a schema key, not data, not published. RIGHT.** `Symbol.for('objectstack.stack.artifact-flow-claims')`, non-enumerable, non-writable, non-configurable, stamped after `markStackProvenance`. `markStackProvenance` always returns an extensible object (the fresh parse result, or a shallow copy of a non-extensible one), so the `Object.isExtensible` early return in `recordArtifactFlowClaims` is unreachable for the producer's own output — a dead branch, not a live fail-open. The readers (`artifactFlowClaimsOf`, `providedFlowNames`, `collectArtifactFlowClaimErrors`) are module-private; nothing new leaves the package entry. The fence test pins `Object.keys` and `JSON.stringify` unchanged.
5. **`composeStacks` — a new refusal reachable only through the new option; not a narrowing. RIGHT.** Step 3b appends `collectArtifactFlowClaimErrors(stacks)`: a recorded claim no input provides is refused with `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID` / 422 and the per-stack message. Before this diff such a stack never reached composition (it was refused at `defineStack`), so nothing previously accepted becomes refused. The existing `collectArtifactCrossReferenceErrors` re-runs only the two object rules (`collectSeedDataObjectErrors`, `collectPermissionGrantObjectErrors`), never `validateCrossReferences`, so an opted-in sibling flow target is not re-refused at composition. The single-input early return (`stacks.length === 1`) precedes step 3b, so the docblock's "a one-package composition leaves the claim unverified" is true of the code. A copy that drops the symbol drops the provenance mark with it, and step 0 refuses an unmarked input (`StackProvenanceMissingError`) — the hunk's "composeStacks already refuses such inputs" holds.
6. **Nested multi-package input. RIGHT.** `providedFlowNames` reads `flows` and `packages[].manifest.flows`; `preservePackageEntries` emits `{ manifest: assemblePackageBody(stack) }` and `assembledPackageBodyShape` carries every concat collection, `flows` included, so a preserve-composed input whose flattened `flows` step 8 deleted still provides them. Pinned.
7. **`widget-dataset-unknown` (lint) — resolution widened, judged set unchanged. RIGHT.** The `datasets` map gains each `packagesOf(stack)` entry's `manifest.datasets`, own declaration first (`!datasets.has`). The dataset-level loop (`measure-aggregate-incoherent`) still iterates `recordsOf(stack.datasets)`; widget-level checks judge the resolved sibling dataset's measures and dimensions (pinned). `packagesOf` throws on `packages: null`, but the same rule table already calls it on the same stack (`validate-object-references.ts`), so no door gains a refusal. The CLI's `packageBodyAsStack` already spreads `packages: artifactPackageEntries` onto each per-package stack — `packages/cli` is correctly untouched.
8. **Runtime publish gate — unchanged. RIGHT.** Neither `runtime-gate.ts` nor `runtime-authoring-gate.ts` builds a `packages` key on the judged stack (the only matches are prose paths), so `packagesOf` answers an empty list there and the rule behaves as before.
9. **Docs. RIGHT.** `content/docs/getting-started/examples.mdx` gains one bullet beside the `artifactObjects` paragraph, in the hand-written tree; `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`, the only other `artifactObjects` mention, is RELEASE-OWNED and correctly untouched. No governed path in the file list; no `skills/**` text to keep in step.

No derived judgment in the diff is wrong.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25514-artifact-flow-dataset-refs.md` declares `'@objectstack/spec': minor` and `'@objectstack/lint': minor` — exactly the two released packages the diff moves (both 18.1.0, neither private). The two declarations are line-initial in the changeset and in the PR body and agree: the `Clause-②:` line reads `yes (widening)` and the `Metadata-protocol:` line reads `added`. `added` is right — a new key an author writes in a `defineStack` call, and a widget binding newly accepted — and a kind takes at least `minor` on a moved package, so the level matches what the diff publishes. The `(widening)` arm is right: judgment 5's compose-time refusal is reachable only through the new option, so no `(narrowing)` arm is owed — unlike #18202, whose re-run design declared a `strict: false` narrowing. No BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 marker are owed. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 6382768493 — one `open_questions` entry and two `out_of_scope_findings` — plus the ruling's two notes and the card's acceptance rows, each answered or escalated:

- **Open question — a recorded claim (A, implemented) vs the `artifactObjects`-style re-run (B): A is right; answered, not escalated.** B would newly refuse a dangling flow target in a `strict: false` input at composition — a narrowing this card's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` does not carry and ruling 6377677280 did not ask for. The reason the `artifactObjects` pass gives for not recording (a composition-time concern on `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`) does not apply to a non-enumerable symbol beside the provenance mark. The record holds exactly what the option let through; it is lost only together with the mark, and composition refuses an unmarked input. The leniency path (own `flows` empty) records no claim because nothing was relied on — consistent. Two mechanisms in one family is an implementation difference each docblock explains, not a contract fork: accept set, envelope and message are one shape.
- **Finding 1 — `indexObjectGraph` reads `stack.objects` alone, so on the per-package pass a widget bound to a sibling dataset whose object is also sibling-owned has its dashboard-filter and widget-filter field checks skipped as unknowable, never refused.** Not a defect at any door (a skip is not a wrong answer) and the existing rung-① design of the per-package pass; the union run judges the union's objects. Prime Directive #10 puts it in the PR's acceptance notes, which the dev could not amend (body write-once): the owning seat should append it there. Not escalated.
- **Finding 2 — HotCRM must add `artifactFlows` to its app package's `defineStack` call.** The card's acceptance row 1 says the hotcrm#2270 patch "validates and builds unchanged"; the flow half needs that one line, the dataset half none. The card's own Ask names the pattern ("the way `artifactObjects` is verified"), which is opt-in by construction: at `defineStack` time a package cannot see its siblings, and deferring the per-stack refusal to composition would widen `defineStack` for every single-package stack, which no ruling asked for. The PR body's acceptance notes disclose it. Carrier: the hotcrm#2270 seat; the maintainer can object in one word. Not escalated.
- **Ruling note 1 (same-artifact only):** honoured — `collectArtifactFlowClaimErrors` resolves against the composition's own inputs; nothing reaches across artifacts, and #25403's territory is untouched.
- **Ruling note 2 (one booted measurement):** present in the PR body, on a temporary extension of `examples/app-multi-package` — the app package's action started the module package's flow (HTTP 200, one `crm_order` row written) and the app widget's module-owned dataset answered its rows. The card's HotCRM rows are measured downstream on a release, as the ruling says.
- **Card acceptance "a regression pin per class, both directions":** `stack-artifact-flow-crossref.test.ts` (9) and `validate-widget-bindings.artifact-datasets.test.ts` (6) pin accept and refuse for both classes, the three flow positions included.
- **Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-24T10:21Z:** every concluded run is `success` or `skipped`; none failed. Still not concluded at this reading: `Test Core (3/6)`, `Test Core (4/6)`, `Test Core (5/6)` — all `in_progress`. `Test Core` is a required context, so this PASS does not make the head green by itself; the owning seat lands only once every required run concludes `success`.
- **The maintainer's no-landing word stands.** The PR is draft under 「正在发版本，你可以派发但是不要合并。」; this record is the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review of record for this head and lifts nothing else. Nothing here readies, queues or arms it.
